content: {"entries":[{"revises":[],"knowledge":[{"text":"The initial Skill's hold-and-apply heat/cool guidance was associated with avoiding door-toggling failures when the required object had been acquired. In the same heat-egg/countertop pair, P9 moved egg1 into microwave1 at P9:14 and then repeatedly opened and closed the microwave through P9:50 without applying heat, ending at the step limit; Q9 heated egg1 while holding it at Q9:7, moved it to countertop1 at Q9:9, and succeeded in 9 steps. Corresponding parents P3, P4, and P8 also eventually applied correct transformations and succeeded, while Q3, Q4, and Q8 did so and succeeded; Q4 and Q8 applied cool/heat while the fridge or microwave was closed at Q4:6 and Q8:5. Thus those pairs preserve the sequence rather than isolate an improvement, whereas the P9/Q9 local difference is specifically door toggling versus hold-and-apply under a joint Skill installation. The clause was not sufficient: in the heat-mug/coffeemachine task Q10 repeatedly heated cup1, the wrong object type, while P10 moved the required mug4 into microwave1 and toggled its door; both hit the step limit.","evidence":["diff","P9:14","P9:15","P9:16","P9:50","Q9:7","Q9:9","P3:8","Q3:7","Q3:9","P4:45","Q4:5","Q4:6","Q4:8","P8:12","Q8:4","Q8:5","Q8:8","P10:45","P10:47","P10:50","Q10:39","Q10:44","Q10:50"]},{"text":"The initial Skill's object-type matching clause was followed in some acquired-target cases but was not reliably enforced. When the matching target was encountered, Q4 took bread1 at Q4:4, Q8 took apple1 at Q8:3, and Q9 took egg1 at Q9:4, and each completed the required transformation and placement. However, in the cool-pot/countertop task Q7 took and moved pan1 at Q7:7-Q7:8 even though the task named pot, then reached the correct pot2 only at Q7:49 and ran out of steps. In the heat-mug/coffeemachine task Q10 took cup1 at Q10:25 and repeatedly heated it at Q10:39 and Q10:44, while P10, on the same task instance, found and took the required mug4 on countertop3 at P10:42; Q10 never reached that object and hit the step limit. In the cool-pan/stoveburner task Q5 saw pot1 on stoveburner1 at Q5:5 and did not take it, consistent with type matching, but P5 instead took pot1 at P5:28, neither side acquired a pan, and both hit the step limit, leaving target availability unresolved.","evidence":["diff","Q4:4","Q8:3","Q9:4","Q7:7","Q7:8","Q7:49","Q7:50","Q10:25","Q10:39","Q10:44","P10:42","Q10:50","Q5:5","P5:28","P5:50","Q5:50"]},{"text":"The initial Skill's search guidance had a large near-surface benefit but did not ensure systematic coverage or avoid rechecking loops. For cool bread/countertop, P4 found bread1 only on diningtable1 at P4:41 and finished in 47 steps, while Q4 reached diningtable1 by Q4:3, took bread1 at Q4:4, and finished in 8. For hot apple/fridge, P8 found apple1 on diningtable1 at P8:8 and finished in 14, while Q8 reached diningtable1 at Q8:2 and finished in 8. In contrast, for cool plate/diningtable, P6 opened cabinet9 at P6:37, took plate1 at P6:38, and finished in 43, while Q6 cycled among countertop1/2, cabinet1/2, and drawer1/2, emitted inadmissible go-to-cabinet3 actions at Q6:6, Q6:23, Q6:29, Q6:40, and Q6:47, never opened cabinet9, and hit the 50-step limit. For cool pot/countertop, P7 took pot2 from stoveburner4 by P7:16 and finished in 20 steps, while Q7 reached pot2 only at Q7:49 and ran out after Q7:50. In P2/Q2 and P5/Q5 both sides hit the step limit without acquiring the named target, leaving target availability and search effectiveness unresolved.","evidence":["diff","P4:41","P4:47","Q4:3","Q4:4","Q4:8","P8:8","P8:14","Q8:2","Q8:8","P6:37","P6:38","P6:43","Q6:6","Q6:23","Q6:29","Q6:40","Q6:47","Q6:50","P7:16","P7:20","Q7:49","Q7:50","P2:50","Q2:50","P5:50","Q5:50"]},{"text":"The initial Skill's action-format clause was associated with fewer malformed commands in several candidate runs but was not reliably followed. Q2 used only admissible commands through Q2:50, while P2 emitted empty or reasoning-text actions at P2:1, P2:2, P2:6, P2:18, P2:29, P2:32, and P2:47; both nevertheless hit the step limit without acquiring bread. Q4's recorded actions included no malformed command and it finished in 8 steps versus P4's 47, although P4 also emitted malformed actions at P4:4, P4:28, and P4:32 and the routes differed, so the step difference is not attributable to format alone. Yet Q6 repeatedly emitted inadmissible go-to-cabinet3 at Q6:6, Q6:23, Q6:29, Q6:40, and Q6:47, and Q7 emitted inadmissible go-to-stoveburner2 at Q7:17 and Q7:46, so the clause did not guarantee valid actions or completion.","evidence":["diff","Q2:49","Q2:50","P2:1","P2:2","P2:6","P2:18","P2:29","P2:32","P2:47","P2:50","Q4:8","P4:47","P4:4","P4:28","P4:32","Q6:6","Q6:23","Q6:29","Q6:40","Q6:47","Q7:17","Q7:46"]},{"text":"For the clean-and-place task, the initial Skill preserved the required acquire, clean at sinkbasin, and place sequence when the matching object was acquired. Both P1 and Q1 took spoon1, cleaned it at sinkbasin1, and moved it to diningtable1; Q1 succeeded in 10 steps versus P1's 9 because Q1 first visited empty countertop1. This pair supports preservation of the clean sequence but, being one pair with an extra initial search step, does not isolate a search-clause cost or benefit.","evidence":["diff","P1:5","P1:7","P1:9","Q1:1","Q1:6","Q1:8","Q1:10"]}]}]}
